title: Parseval identity for a Walsh polynomial
statement: For any natural number $n$ and any real coefficient family $p$ indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the uniform inner product of the polynomial represented by $p$ with itself equals $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of the coordinate set
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. Then $\mathbb E[P(x)P(x)]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S^2$.
